For T≤t_0 no positive saving is possible (a terminal purge ties no purge); for T>t_0 the positive product is strictly log-concave between its zeros. At T/2 its logarithmic derivative is positive if that point is already in the beneficial interval. The implicit derivative is A/(A−(log D)″), where A=a²exp(a(T−τ))/(exp(a(T−τ))−1)²>0. At onset the stationarity equation is 1/y−1/(ε−y)+O(1)=0, which gives y=ε/2+O(ε²) and the stated quadratic savings. The midpoint test forces both optimal lead and lag to diverge; balancing the two marginal exponential tails then gives the constant timing offset and residual coefficient. Equal rates give an exact geometric balance. For fixed T, the objective converges uniformly on [0,T] as x↓0 to the symmetric objective with unique maximizer T/2, justifying the iterated limits.
